ov: Not a single group but 91 species of horned, hoofed bovids, most of them native to Africa. They are only distantly related to deer: antelope horns are bone covered in keratin, grow steadily and are never shed, unlike antlers.

why.et: Hunted for meat, and ancient Egyptians kept herds of gazelles and addax for it.

ht: 24 cm (royal antelope) to 178 cm (eland) at the shoulder
rg: Most of Africa, the Middle East, India, Central Asia and a small area of Russia.
fx: The pronghorn, often called the American antelope, belongs to a different family.
Africa has only one living deer species, but 25–40 antelope species share much of East Africa.
